models.composition: Le Rhône et la Saône — André Vermare
models.qualification: Museum record2015.0.13/FNAC1688 and municipal library identify the same1901–1905 Carrara marble high relief installed at Palais de la Bourse, Lyon,1907. Actually compared the source thumbnail with the museum's Alain Basset physical photograph: all two adult figures, faces, crossed/reaching arms, shoulders, torso, legs, rocks, wave ridges, irregular relief edge and lettered lower support match. Count the entire relief as one work; no component figures or plaster/bronze versions as additional compositions. Museum dimensions156×330×80cm are documentary only, not digital calibration. Native inspection must verify the entire right-reaching hand, opposing arm, both figures' limbs, fractured-looking stone areas, irregular top/background boundary and captured paving. Do not reconstruct relief backs as independent geometry. Exact metadata is downloadable CC BY4 and isAiGenerated:false. ROOT adult curation, source acquisition, native and eight-direction paired rendering, final preview and private archive remain pending; no bodies fetched by this research.

models.composition: Votive Relief with Reclining Herakles — Unknown Roman sculptor, after a Hellenistic work
models.qualification: The museum's official exhibit list identifies votive relief1454 in room34. Actually matched the source thumbnail to the physical NAMA1454 photograph: bearded face, reclining torso and pelvis, raised/broken right wrist, left hand position, lion head/pelt, long crossed legs and irregular tall background break all agree. Museum-label transcription describes a Roman2nd-centuryCE copy of an earlier Hellenistic relief, found at MonastirakiSquare in Athens; preserve that copy distinction and the historical broken forearm/hand and background edges. Do not merge this relief with standing/Farnese/Lansdowne Herakles or with different banquet reliefs. The official list verifies inventory/type, while the dated copy/findspot wording is corroborated by a physical museum-label transcription, not an invented online museum object description. Keep the mounting base and label/capture limits qualified. Physical scale remains uncalibrated. Exact metadata is downloadable CC BY4 and isAiGenerated:false. models.composition: Léto (Summer), also recorded as Woman with a Rose — Václav Kyselka
models.qualification: The primary university art-in-public-space registry identifies the exact Truhlářova/Střekov sculpture as Léto,1983, sandstone, by Václav Kyselka, with architect Vladislav Valoušek and contributor Petr Veselý. The publisher's Woman with a Rose is an alternate name, and its1970s date is superseded by the primary1983 record. Actually matched physical photograph and scan: raised folded arms, hair, breast/abdomen, lowered drapery, knees, feet, integral base, long vertical weathering and conspicuous blue paint mark on the left abdomen. Retain the paint/weathering rather than retouching. University dimensions195×50×60cm are documentary only, not digital calibration. The current Kyselka Ball Games and Married Couple records are distinct compositions. Native review must verify fingers/overlapping hands, hair, breast surfaces, drapery, both feet and base boundary. Exact model metadata is downloadable and isAiGenerated:false, with the pinned model-level license. ROOT adult curation, acquisition, native/paired/final review and archive remain pending. No body acquired by this research.
